creator: ducktate.com
title: Pricing retention 'hack': a Pro plan that gets slightly cheaper every month you stay (e.g. $29.99 -> $29.50 -> $29) but resets to full price on cancel, creating loss-aversion friction; creator plans to add it to his app Ducktate

tools.name: Ducktate (creator's app)
tools.detail: ducktate.com handle; 'Hacks from building an app' episode 2

claims: Every subscription follows the same 3-tier pattern (free, pro, yearly) and has an 'absurd' amount of churn
Decreasing-price loyalty plan makes users 'almost refuse' to cancel because cancelling resets the price to full
Attributed to an unnamed founder ('this guy')
how_to_steps: Make the Pro price decay a small amount each consecutive month subscribed (e.g. $29.99, $29.50, $29.00...)
On cancellation, reset the user's price to the full list price so re-subscribing costs more
Surface the user's earned discount at cancel time to create friction
on_screen_only: Title card 'HACKS FROM BUILDING AN APP — EPISODE 2'
Word-by-word subtitles only; no app UI, pricing page or billing code shown
cta: follow for the daily series ('see you tomorrow')

relevance.why: A pricing/retention tactic relevant to any subscription app Haji ships, but presented without data, source, or implementation details (Stripe/RevenueCat handling); dark-pattern adjacent and needs legal review

implement_score.why: Could be implemented with Stripe coupons/subscription schedules (tenure-based discount) in a day, but the loss-aversion-on-cancel mechanic may conflict with FTC click-to-cancel / consumer-protection rules and could hurt trust; test as a loyalty discount first, without the punitive reset

gap.what: New tactic: tenure-based decaying subscription price with reset-on-cancel as a churn lever. Liked set covered legal/compliance checklists and app UX but not pricing/retention mechanics

verify: Who actually runs this model and what are their churn numbers?
Legal: does a price reset on cancel violate FTC Negative Option/click-to-cancel rules or app-store subscription policies (Apple/Google require clear pricing)?
Does Stripe/RevenueCat support per-tenure price decay natively or does it require custom coupon logic?
Does the decaying price materially reduce LTV versus the churn it prevents?
